metadata.name: Indian Patent Rules Database
metadata.important_note: Legal provisions must be verified against the latest Gazette and official IP India sources before making filing or prosecution decisions.

rules.title: Non-patentable inventions
rules.requirement: The claimed subject matter should be screened for exclusions from patentability under Section 3 of the Patents Act.

rules.title: Frivolous or contrary to natural laws
rules.requirement: The invention should not be frivolous or obviously contrary to well established natural laws.

rules.title: Public order and morality
rules.requirement: Subject matter should be screened for exclusion where its primary or intended use or commercial exploitation would be contrary to public order or morality or harmful to specified protected interests.

rules.title: Mere discovery
rules.requirement: A mere discovery of a scientific principle or formulation of an abstract theory or discovery of a living or non-living substance occurring in nature is excluded.

rules.title: New form of known substance
rules.requirement: For relevant pharmaceutical or chemical subject matter, the claim should be screened against the requirements and exclusions relating to new forms of known substances and enhanced efficacy.

rules.title: Mere admixture
rules.requirement: A mere admixture resulting only in aggregation of properties of components should be screened for exclusion under Section 3(e).

rules.title: Mere arrangement or duplication
rules.requirement: A mere arrangement or re-arrangement or duplication of known devices functioning independently should be screened under Section 3(f).

rules.title: Traditional subject matter
rules.requirement: Subject matter falling within the specified exclusion relating to methods of agriculture or horticulture should be screened accordingly.

rules.title: Methods of treatment
rules.requirement: Methods of medicinal, surgical, curative, prophylactic, diagnostic or therapeutic treatment of humans or animals should be screened against the exclusion under Section 3(h).

rules.title: Treatment methods
rules.requirement: Claims directed to treatment of humans or animals should be specifically screened for statutory exclusion.

rules.title: Plants and animals
rules.requirement: Plants and animals in whole or part, seeds, varieties and species and essentially biological processes for production or propagation should be screened against the applicable exclusion.

rules.title: Computer programme per se
rules.requirement: Computer programme per se and mathematical methods should be screened against the applicable exclusions. Computer-related inventions require careful assessment of the claimed subject matter.

rules.title: Literary, dramatic, musical or artistic work
rules.requirement: Literary, dramatic, musical or artistic works and certain other aesthetic creations should be screened for statutory exclusion.

rules.title: Scheme or rule or method of performing mental act
rules.requirement: Schemes, rules or methods for performing mental acts and related excluded subject matter should be screened.

rules.title: Presentation of information
rules.requirement: A mere presentation of information should be screened for the applicable statutory exclusion.

rules.title: Topography of integrated circuits
rules.requirement: Topography of integrated circuits should be screened against the relevant exclusion.

rules.title: Traditional knowledge
rules.requirement: An invention which is in effect traditional knowledge or which aggregates or duplicates known properties of traditionally known components should be screened for exclusion.

rules.title: Atomic energy
rules.requirement: Inventions relating to atomic energy should be screened for the statutory prohibition and applicable restrictions.

rules.title: Information regarding foreign applications
rules.requirement: Where applicable, applicants are required to provide information concerning corresponding foreign applications in accordance with Section 8 and the applicable Rules.

rules.title: Statement and undertaking regarding foreign applications
rules.requirement: Information and undertaking relating to foreign applications must be handled in accordance with the applicable Rule 12 requirements and Form 3 procedure.

rules.title: Provisional and complete specification
rules.requirement: Where a provisional specification is filed, the complete specification must subsequently comply with the applicable statutory requirements and prescribed time limits.

rules.title: Title and description
rules.requirement: Every specification shall describe the invention and begin with a title sufficiently indicating the subject matter to which the invention relates.

rules.title: Full and particular description
rules.requirement: A complete specification shall fully and particularly describe the invention, its operation or use and the method by which it is to be performed.

rules.title: Best method
rules.requirement: The complete specification shall disclose the best method of performing the invention which is known to the applicant and for which protection is claimed.

rules.title: Claims define scope
rules.requirement: The complete specification shall end with one or more claims defining the scope of the invention for which protection is claimed.

rules.title: Single invention or linked group
rules.requirement: Claims should relate to a single invention or to a group of inventions linked so as to form a single inventive concept.

rules.title: Claims clear and succinct
rules.requirement: Claims should be clear and succinct and should be fairly based on the matter disclosed in the specification.

rules.title: Abstract
rules.requirement: The complete specification shall be accompanied by an abstract of the invention.

rules.title: Specification in Form 2
rules.requirement: Every provisional or complete specification shall be made in Form 2.

rules.title: Drawings and reference signs
rules.requirement: Where drawings are necessary for explanation of the invention, they should comply with Rule 15 and be referred to in detail in the specification; relevant features in drawings should use reference signs where applicable.

rules.title: Irrelevant matter
rules.requirement: Irrelevant or unnecessary matter should be excluded from the title, description, claims and drawings.

rules.title: Abstract requirements
rules.requirement: The abstract should provide a concise summary of the matter contained in the specification, including the technical field, technical advancement if any, and principal use or uses.

rules.title: Abstract word limit
rules.requirement: The abstract should not contain more than 150 words.

rules.title: Abstract as search instrument
rules.requirement: The abstract should be drafted so that it can serve as an efficient instrument for searching the particular art.

rules.title: Drawing format
rules.requirement: Drawings supplied with specifications should comply with the applicable Rule 15 requirements, including prescribed sheet format, margins, numbering and presentation requirements.

rules.title: A4 drawing sheets
rules.requirement: Drawings should be prepared on standard A4 size sheets with the prescribed clear margins.

rules.title: Drawing scale
rules.requirement: Drawings should be on a scale sufficiently large to show the invention clearly and dimensions should not be marked on the drawings.

rules.title: Drawing identification
rules.requirement: Drawings should be sequentially or systematically numbered and carry the prescribed applicant, sheet and signature information.

rules.title: Request for examination
rules.requirement: A request for examination must be filed within the applicable period prescribed under Rule 24B, subject to transitional provisions and the date of filing.

rules.title: Current examination period
rules.requirement: For applications governed by the current rule, the request for examination is generally subject to the thirty-one-month period specified in Rule 24B, with transitional provisions for older applications.

rules.title: Expedited examination
rules.requirement: Where expedited examination is sought, the applicant must satisfy the applicable eligibility and procedural requirements under Rule 24C.

rules.title: Publication of application
rules.requirement: Patent applications are subject to the publication provisions of Section 11A, subject to applicable exceptions and procedures.

rules.title: Request for examination
rules.requirement: An application is not examined unless the prescribed request for examination is made in accordance with Section 11B and the applicable Rules.

rules.title: Search for anticipation
rules.requirement: Examination includes consideration of whether the invention is anticipated by prior publication or prior claiming in accordance with the Act.

rules.title: Consideration of examiner report
rules.requirement: The Controller considers the examiner's report and applicable objections during examination proceedings.

rules.title: Power of Controller
rules.requirement: The Controller may refuse or require amendment of an application or specification where the statutory requirements are not met, subject to the Act and Rules.

rules.title: Divisional applications
rules.requirement: Where multiple inventions are disclosed in an application, the applicability of divisional filing under Section 16 may need consideration.

rules.title: Further applications
rules.requirement: The 2024 amendment introduced Rule 13(2A), permitting an applicant, if desired, to file one or more further applications under Section 16 in the circumstances specified.

rules.title: Amendment of application and specification
rules.requirement: Amendments to applications or specifications must comply with the statutory requirements governing amendment.

rules.title: Limitations on amendment
rules.requirement: Amendments to a specification should remain within the statutory limits and should not introduce matter beyond the original disclosure.

rules.title: Computer-related inventions
rules.requirement: Computer-related inventions should be analyzed against the applicable statutory exclusion and the current official CRI examination guidelines. The analysis should focus on the substance and technical contribution rather than merely the wording of the claim.

rules.title: Excluded subject matter screening
rules.requirement: The analyzer should identify claim features that may correspond to statutory exclusions, but should not automatically conclude that an invention is excluded without sufficient technical and legal context.

rules.title: Anticipation procedure
rules.requirement: Potential anticipation issues should be considered in accordance with the applicable procedure under Rule 28A.

rules.title: Anticipation by prior claiming
rules.requirement: Potential anticipation by prior claiming should be considered in accordance with Rule 29.

rules.title: Grace period
rules.requirement: Where relevant, the analyzer should identify whether the facts potentially require consideration of the statutory grace-period provisions under Rule 29A.

rules.title: Amendment in anticipation cases
rules.requirement: Where anticipation issues arise, amendments to the complete specification are subject to the applicable procedure under Rule 30.

rules.title: Extension and condonation of delay
rules.requirement: Where an applicant seeks extension of time or condonation of delay, the applicable requirements of Rule 138 and its exclusions should be checked.

rules.title: 2024 amendments
rules.requirement: The analyzer should account for applicable amendments introduced by the Patents (Amendment) Rules, 2024 and Patents (Second Amendment) Rules, 2024, while recognizing transitional provisions.

rules.title: Updated foreign application information
rules.requirement: The 2024 amendments modified Rule 12 procedures relating to information concerning applications filed outside India, including specified timelines and Form 4 requests for applicable extensions or condonation.

rules.title: Updated request-for-examination period
rules.requirement: The 2024 amendment changed the applicable request-for-examination period to thirty-one months for applications governed by the amended provision, while preserving transitional treatment for certain earlier applications.
